name: Eastern Visayas
summary_text: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. The attached sources are national-level rather than regional: a country-organisation overview of the national legal picture, a June 2025 report on the killing of an 18-year-old trans woman in a different province (Cagayan), and a national news item on a case in another region (Batangas) that could not be retrieved at fetch time.

sources.title: Philippines | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International's Philippines country overview (updated 12 March 2026): same-sex conduct legal nationwide; no legal gender recognition (still required: no LGR pathway); Executive Order 100 s.2019 (signed 17 Dec 2019) created a Diversity and Inclusion Program, amended by EO 51 s.2023 to add a special LGBTQIA+ affairs committee, neither implemented as of 2025; anti-discrimination ordinances exist at barangay, city, municipal and provincial levels but national legislation filed since 1999 has not been enacted; a 2018 Social Weather Stations survey found 22% support for same-sex civil unions and a majority opposed trans women's access to women's toilets.

sources.title: Recent killings of trans women prompt groups to push for LGBTQIA protection
sources.claim_summary: Alternative-media report (26 June 2025): an 18-year-old trans woman, Kierra Apostol, was found dead with signs of physical assault in a river in Peñablanca, Cagayan province on 23 June 2025 after being missing since 22 June; her mother reported the disappearance to local police; Bahaghari (national LGBT alliance) chairperson called the killing part of a pattern of violence against Filipino trans women and renewed calls for the SOGIESC Equality Bill. Case is in Cagayan Valley region, not Eastern Visayas — national-climate evidence.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 403); the underlying national-news article covers the arrest of a foreign national for raping a trans woman in Batangas (May 2025), cited for the national picture of violence against trans women; the case is in another region, not Eastern Visayas.
